compiled_state.description: Observed 2026-09-10 in a Copilot CLI session on the rebar checkout: the configured rebar MCP server is absent from the session's available tools; the client surfaces 'MCP server rebar requires authentication. Use /mcp auth rebar to connect.' The agent only discovers the degradation indirectly (missing tools) and falls back to the local rebar CLI carve-out for all tracker ops, which works but bypasses the MCP routing policy in AGENTS.md (certified ops signed under the box's trusted signing environment, async gate starters, de-dup protection) and makes every tracker op slower. Impact: tracker writes/gates from Copilot sessions are un-certified relative to the on-box MCP path; if opcert environment enforcement (verify.require_environment + verify.opcert_enforce_since) is ever flipped on per ADR 0104, these sessions' gate ops would stop being acceptable. Acceptance criteria: (1) root-cause why the Copilot CLI session's rebar MCP auth is not established (expired/absent token vs. auth flow requiring interactive /mcp auth each session vs. server-side config; see docs/mcp-auth.md and docs/mcp-client-setup.md); (2) make auth durable for non-interactive agent sessions on this host, or document the sanctioned per-session auth step in the machine-local setup notes; (3) verify a fresh Copilot CLI session lists the rebar MCP tools and completes one read (show) and one write (comment) through MCP. Related: 9ea3-7d07-ea55-4496 (remote MCP endpoint 502) for prior MCP-availability defects.
compiled_state.title: Copilot CLI session cannot use configured rebar MCP server: connection requires authentication ('/mcp auth rebar') that a non-interactive agent session never completes, silently degrading to local-CLI fallback
